gloss: to read through, to read from beginning to end

definitions.gloss: to read through, to read from beginning to end
definitions.explanation: To read an entire text from start to finish without skipping parts. Implies a complete, continuous reading rather than skimming or selective reading.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}を{通読|つうどく}する。
まず{全体|ぜんたい}を{通読|つうどく}してから{細部|さいぶ}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I first read through the whole thing, then checked the details.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{一気|いっき}に{通読|つうどく}できるほど{面白|おもしろ}かった。
examples.english: This novel was so interesting that I could read it straight through in one sitting.

notes:
Emphasizes reading a text in its entirety without skipping. Often used in academic, professional, or literary contexts to describe thorough reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一気|いっき}に{通読|つうどく}する: to read through in one sitting
- {全文|ぜんぶん}を{通読|つうどく}する: to read the full text through
- {通読|つうどく}に{値|あたい}する: worth reading through

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {読破|どくは}する: to finish reading — emphasizes completing a challenging or long text
- {精読|せいどく}する: to read carefully — emphasizes close, detailed analysis
- {速読|そくどく}する: to speed-read — emphasizes reading quickly
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}み: skimming — the opposite approach; reading selectively
